question: 1. Does vercel.json redirects permanent:true return 308? How to force 301? Do Google/browsers treat 301 and 308 the same?
answer: permanent:true (the default) returns 308; permanent:false returns 307. Use "statusCode": 301 (integer; cannot be combined with permanent) to emit 301. Compiling a vercel.json with statusCode 301 through @vercel/routing-utils and through real `vercel build` yields a route with status 301. Google documents 301 and 308 as the permanent pair and treats both as a canonical signal; per Vercel docs both are cached by clients. 301 may change POST to GET, irrelevant for page and feed GETs.
evidence_url_or_command: https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#redirects (permanent table row: 'status code is 308'; statusCode row; example { source:/user, destination:/api/user, statusCode:301 }); https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects ('The 301 and 308 status codes mean that a page has permanently moved'); local: node t2.mjs in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-johnsolly-code-jsolly-website/8907a598-cb6b-487a-8acb-089323998de1/scratchpad/merge-plan/clones/platform/routing-utils printed {"status":301} for statusCode:301; `vercel build` in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-johnsolly-code-jsolly-website/8907a598-cb6b-487a-8acb-089323998de1/scratchpad/merge-plan/clones/platform/jsolly-website (config.json route 6-8 status 301)
plan_implication: Every legacy redirect in the map uses "statusCode": 301 (never permanent:true, which would give 308). The redirect-coverage test must assert status === 301 exactly, not just 3xx. Note the platform's own hops stay 308 (http->https, apex->www, trailing-slash); only our per-path rules can be 301, so a chain that includes a platform hop is mixed 308/301, which Google treats identically.

question: 2. With trailingSlash:true, is the trailing-slash 308 applied BEFORE redirects (two hops)? Best source pattern to match both slash forms in one hop? Evaluation order among redirects, http->https and apex->www?
answer: YES, two hops. Real `vercel build` of jsolly-website compiles routes in this order: [0-1 _astro cache headers] [2 .well-known passthrough] [3 add-trailing-slash 308 for paths with no dot: ^/((?:[^/]+/)*[^/\.]+)$ -> /$1/] [4 strip-slash 308 for file-extension paths] [5 vercel.json redirects in array order] [6 headers, continue] [7 middleware] then filesystem/rewrites. Live proof on a site with the same setting (awesome-blog, trailingSlash:true + a vercel.json redirect): GET /post/how-to-leverage-closed-loops (no slash) -> 308 /post/how-to-leverage-closed-loops/ and only then 308 to the destination. Redirect rules are evaluated in array order, first match wins (live: awesome-blog lists two specific redirects before its catch-all apex->www rule and https://blogthedata.com/post/how-to-leverage-closed-loops/ goes straight to the destination on the apex host). Pattern syntax: path-to-regexp (v6.1.0 in routing-utils). Valid single-rule patterns matching both slash forms: "/post/:slug{/}?" -> ^/post(?:/([^/]+?))(?:/)?$ and "/post/foo{/}?" and "/post/foo(/)?". INVALID (rejected by the compiler): "/post/foo/?", "/post/:slug/?", "/post/(foo)/?". But under trailingSlash:true the no-slash form never reaches the rule because route 3 fires first. http->https is a platform 308 on the same host that happens before everything (live: http://blogthedata.com/... -> 308 https://blogthedata.com/...). apex->www: a domain-level redirect or a vercel.json host rule; jsolly.com/about -> 308 https://www.jsolly.com/about (no slash added) then www /about -> 308 /about/ (live, 3 hops total from http://jsolly.com/about).
evidence_url_or_command: File: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-johnsolly-code-jsolly-website/8907a598-cb6b-487a-8acb-089323998de1/scratchpad/merge-plan/clones/platform/jsolly-website/.vercel/output/config.json (generated by `npx vercel build --yes --prod` offline, route indexes 2-7); live: curl -sI https://www.blogthedata.com/post/how-to-leverage-closed-loops (308 -> slash form), curl -sI https://jsolly.com/about, http://jsolly.com/about; compiler output /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-johnsolly-code-jsolly-website/8907a598-cb6b-487a-8acb-089323998de1/scratchpad/merge-plan/clones/platform/routing-utils/t2.mjs; docs https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json#trailingslash ('visiting a path that does not end with a forward slash will respond with a 308')
plan_implication: Hosting legacy redirects inside jsolly-website's vercel.json (which must keep trailingSlash:true) cannot give one hop for no-slash legacy URLs: 301 only after a 308 slash hop. A separate redirect-only project WITHOUT trailingSlash set uses one rule `/post/:slug{/}?` per path and gets one hop for both slash forms and both hosts. Source patterns must be generated with escaping for ( ) [ ] { } ? * + : \ in slugs and tested by compiling with getTransformedRoutes (invalid patterns return an error object, they do not throw).

question: 3. Is redirect source matching case-sensitive? Any control?
answer: Yes for vercel.json redirects/rewrites/headers: docs say 'the source property is case-sensitive'. The CDN does not lowercase paths ('/About' and '/about' are different; 404 if absent). Live: https://www.blogthedata.com/post/How-To-Leverage-Closed-Loops/ -> 404 while the lowercase form redirects; https://www.jsolly.com/About/ -> 404. There is no case-insensitive option on vercel.json redirects (the compiled routes carry no caseSensitive flag). Bulk redirects and CLI/project-level redirects DO have caseSensitive, default false.
evidence_url_or_command: https://vercel.com/docs/project-configuration/vercel-json (Case sensitivity: 'redirects ... source property is case-sensitive so you don't accidentally create duplicate content'); https://vercel.com/docs/routing/redirects ('Case sensitivity: CDN does not normalize URL paths to lowercase'); live curl probes above
plan_implication: Preserve legacy slug case exactly (e.g. mixed-case post slugs and categories like Geodev): each distinct-case URL that was ever linked needs its own rule or an explicit decision to 404. The URL-map test must include the mixed-case slugs verbatim. Do not rely on a catch-all lowercase normaliser (not available).

question: 4. Are query strings passed through to the destination? Can destination append them? 'has' conditions?
answer: Query strings are passed through automatically, even when the destination has no query: live https://www.blogthedata.com/post/how-to-leverage-closed-loops/?utm_source=x&a=1 -> Location /post/stop-asking-questions-to-save-time/?utm_source=x&a=1; docs: 'Query parameters pass through unless you explicitly replace them in the destination'. A destination that includes its own query replaces the incoming one. 'has' query conditions match request query params (type:query) and are not needed here. Bulk/project-level redirects preserve query only if preserveQueryParams is true (default false).
evidence_url_or_command: live curl (see above); https://vercel.com/docs/routing/redirects#choose-a-canonical-production-domain; https://vercel.com/docs/routing/redirects/bulk-redirects (preserveQueryParams default false)
plan_implication: No special handling is needed for utm_* params on vercel.json redirects. If John ever uses Bulk Redirects, set preserveQueryParams true. Add one test case with a query string to the coverage test.

question: 5. Limits: max redirects in vercel.json; Bulk Redirects (what, from a repo file, status codes, plan)?
answer: vercel.json: 2,048 redirects, 4,096 chars per source/destination. Bulk Redirects: up to 1,000,000 per project, from a committed file via vercel.json "bulkRedirectsPath" (CSV/JSON/JSONL, a file or a folder of up to 100 files) or at runtime via dashboard/API/CLI (`vercel redirects ...`, no redeploy, staged then promoted). No wildcards or header matching. Source may be an absolute path or a fully qualified URL (host-scoped, e.g. https://old.example/page). Status via permanent (308/307) or statusCode 301/302/303/307/308. caseSensitive default false, preserveQueryParams default false. Processed before any other route in the deployment. AVAILABILITY: Pro and Enterprise only (included 1,000 on Pro); NOT on Hobby. This account's billing plan is HOBBY (get_auth_user billing.plan). `vercel build` does not emit bulk redirects into config.json (they are applied by the platform at deploy), so they cannot be unit-tested offline from the build output.

question: 6. Host-conditioned redirects: has type host; match www and apex with one regex?
answer: Supported. has:[{type:'host', value:'...'}] value is a regex-like string that is matched against the full host (live: awesome-blog's rule value 'blogthedata.com' redirects the apex but NOT www.blogthedata.com, which serves 200, so it is anchored). Compiles for alternation: value '(www\.)?blogthedata\.com' compiled into a has-host route (vercel build config.json route 6-8). Vercel's own docs use the escaped form 'your-project\\.vercel\\.app' in JSON. Note `has` does not work under local `vercel dev`, only when deployed. Host conditions cannot be exercised on a preview/*.vercel.app URL (host will not match) and a forged Host header does not select another project's domain, so host-conditioned rules can only be proven in production after the domain is attached.

question: 7. Order of vercel.json redirects/headers vs Routing Middleware (middleware.ts at project root). Do redirects run first? Does middleware run for redirected requests?
answer: Redirects (and the trailing-slash 308s) run BEFORE middleware, and a redirect response terminates routing, so middleware never runs for a redirected request. Real `vercel build` of jsolly-website: route 3-5 are redirects, route 6 sets the global headers (continue), route 7 is the middleware (`middlewarePath: middleware`, continue, override), then the error handler. Consequences: (a) redirect responses carry NONE of the vercel.json headers (headers route comes after redirects), (b) middleware only sees requests that survive redirects. Docs: Bulk Redirects run before everything; Firewall redirects run before config redirects; project-level routing rules run after bulk redirects and before deployment routes; Routing Middleware 'runs before the cache'. Compiled with the experimental legacy rules, order stayed: trailing-slash -> host redirects -> headers -> middleware -> (handle: filesystem) -> rewrites.
evidence_url_or_command: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-johnsolly-code-jsolly-website/8907a598-cb6b-487a-8acb-089323998de1/scratchpad/merge-plan/clones/platform/jsolly-website/.vercel/output/config.json (routes 2-9); https://vercel.com/docs/routing#routing-order; https://vercel.com/docs/routing/redirects#firewall-redirects
plan_implication: Legacy redirects hosted in jsolly-website never hit middleware.ts (good). But all NON-redirect responses for the merged site do go through middleware: see the middleware hazards entry (406 for feed readers on extensionless feed URLs, 404 markdown for .md data files, markdown negotiation for /blog/<slug>/).

question: 8. Two header rules matching a path and setting the same key (e.g. Content-Security-Policy on /(.*) and /blog/(.*)): override or both sent?
answer: Not documented by Vercel. Evidence: both rules compile to separate routes with continue:true (config.json routes 6 and 10 in the experiment), and the open-source Vercel CLI dev router merges continue-route headers with combinedHeaders[lowerCaseKey]=value, i.e. the LATER rule overwrites the earlier one for the same key (single header sent). Next.js documents the same last-wins semantic for its headers() config. If a platform ever sent both, browsers would enforce the intersection of two CSP headers (spec: each policy must be satisfied). Production edge behavior is therefore LIKELY last-wins but UNVERIFIED on the real edge.

Make header sources disjoint (negative lookahead) or, better, move all resource directives into Astro's security.csp (meta tag, merges per page) and keep only frame-ancestors (+ upgrade-insecure-requests) in the single Vercel header. Add a built-output test asserting exactly one Content-Security-Policy header value per path class.

question: 9. Domain-level redirects in Vercel: only blanket? path-preserving? status codes? Can a domain be attached purely for redirects?
answer: Domain redirects (Project > Settings > Domains > Redirect to) redirect one project domain to ANOTHER DOMAIN (the API field 'redirect' is 'Target destination domain for redirect', hostname only, no path) with redirectStatusCode in {301,302,307,308}. They are blanket per host: no per-path mapping, and the destination cannot be a path such as /blog. Docs describe it as e.g. www -> apex, so the original path is carried over, but path-preservation is not stated explicitly (UNVERIFIED). Redirect-only attachment is possible (add the domain to a project and set Redirect to), which is exactly how jsolly.com -> www.jsolly.com is configured today (list_project_domains: jsolly.com redirect www.jsolly.com, redirectStatusCode 308). Because the redirect is unconditional it would also redirect the tombstone service-worker URL.
evidence_url_or_command: https://vercel.com/docs/domains/working-with-domains/deploying-and-redirecting#redirecting-domains; https://vercel.com/docs/rest-api/projects/update-a-project-domain (redirect, redirectStatusCode enum 301/302/307/308); Vercel MCP list_project_domains for jsolly-website
plan_implication: Option D (domain-level redirect) is rejected: blanket host redirect, cannot map to /blog/<slug>/ or /recipes/, redirects the SW URL (an SW script URL that redirects makes the update fail, see SW entry), and still needs path rewrites on the destination host (2 hops).

question: 11. What happens to the production deployment and its vercel.json redirects when the connected GitHub repo is ARCHIVED? Can redirects be changed later without unarchiving? Retention policies?
answer: Vercel documents nothing specific about archived repos (searched docs: none). Reasoning from documented mechanics: an archived GitHub repo is read-only so no further pushes can trigger Git deployments; an existing production deployment is an immutable artifact aliased to the domains and keeps serving; its vercel.json redirects are baked into that deployment. RETENTION: default production retention is 30 days on Hobby (1 year on Pro) BUT a deployment 'has a production alias assigned to it' is an exception on every plan, so the current aliased production deployment is never auto-deleted; Hobby also keeps the last 3 Ready production deployments (rollback candidates). Once superseded, old deployments can be deleted after the retention period (30 days on Hobby) with a 30-day recovery window. CHANGING REDIRECTS WITHOUT UNARCHIVING: possible via (1) Git-less deploy from any checkout: `vercel deploy --prod` (CLI/API deploys do not need the Git integration), (2) project-level Routing Rules or Bulk Redirects (dashboard/API/CLI, no deploy; Bulk is Pro-only), (3) `vercel git disconnect` first so the project is not coupled to an archived repo. Whether Vercel auto-disconnects or warns on an archived repo is UNVERIFIED. The cleaner approach is to change the project's Git source to an ACTIVE repo before archiving.
evidence_url_or_command: https://vercel.com/docs/deployment-retention (table: Hobby production 30 days; exceptions: 'The deployment has a production alias assigned to it', Hobby 'Production deployments in state Ready: Last 3'; 'recovery period 30 days'); https://vercel.com/docs/cli/git (vercel git disconnect); https://vercel.com/docs/cli/deploying-from-cli; Vercel MCP list_deployments for blogthedata (latest production dpl_5BjMTUs5SSu6YFnR8QoJRu6dGHtp from awesome-blog bf1f7ff1, 10+ READY production deployments, isRollbackCandidate true); gh api repos/jsolly/awesome-blog -> id 286148731, archived:false, public
plan_implication: Archiving awesome-blog does not by itself take blogthedata.com down, but an awesome-blog-sourced redirect list would be frozen (edits need unarchive or a manual CLI deploy). Therefore re-point the blogthedata Vercel project to an active repo BEFORE archiving (recommended design). Instant Rollback on HOBBY only reaches the IMMEDIATELY PREVIOUS deployment (docs: 'Hobby users can roll back to the immediately previous deployment'), so the awesome-blog deployment is a rollback target only until the next redirect-only production deployment. Fallback after that, valid only while awesome-blog is NOT yet archived: reconnect the repo to the project and redeploy main (bf1f7ff1), or `vercel deploy --prod` from a checkout of it. This is why archiving must wait until redirects are verified in production and no further redirect-only fixes are pending. Retention (last 3 Ready production deployments on Hobby) is a different rule and does not make older deployments roll-back-able.

question: 12. Astro 7 security.csp: per-page directives in a STATIC build? How is CSP emitted? How do globally-added frame-src/img-src affect jsolly pages?
answer: Per-page CSP works in static builds and is emitted as <meta http-equiv="content-security-policy"> in each page head (astro 7.3.2, jsolly-website scratch build). Tested: Astro.csp?.insertDirective("img-src 'self' https: data:") and insertDirective("frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com") on one page produced those directives ONLY on that page; /about/ kept the global policy. A per-page directive with the same name as a global one is MERGED (global 'img-src self data:' + page 'self https: data:' -> 'img-src self data: https:' on that page only), not duplicated. Directives set in astro.config security.csp.directives apply to ALL pages (so a global frame-src/img-src would loosen every jsolly page). Gotchas found by experiment: (1) script/style HASHES are site-global: every page lists the union of all pages' processed-script hashes. Rigorous check: baseline /about/ meta had 7 sha256 hashes; after adding a page whose only difference is one <script>console.log(...)</script> (emitted as <script type='module'>console.log(`...`);), /about/'s meta had 8 hashes, the new hash 'sha256-ljDi2p1E...' was present in /about/'s meta, and /about/'s HTML does not contain that script (files platform-experiments/hashes-*.txt). Note `is:inline` scripts were NOT hashed at all in this test (hash absent from every meta), so they would be blocked by script-src; (2) insertScriptResource('https://cdn.example.com') alone REPLACED script-src's default 'self' on that page - you must also insert "'self'" explicitly; (3) the emitted meta also carries default-src 'self' and, with the current config, no img-src (so images fall back to default-src 'self' and data: is blocked by the meta, while the Vercel header img-src also allows data:). Current built output (scratch, 7 pages): default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' + 7 sha256; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'.

question: 13. Do CSP meta tags support frame-ancestors / report-uri / sandbox? Implications for keeping frame-ancestors in the Vercel header.
answer: No. CSP3: 'Neither are the report-uri, frame-ancestors, and sandbox directives' supported in a meta-delivered policy; Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only cannot be delivered by meta; a meta policy is enforced along with any other active policy (intersection) and does not apply to content that precedes the meta element. Astro WILL emit those directives into the meta if asked (tested insertDirective("frame-ancestors 'none'") produced them in the tag) but browsers ignore them there, silently losing protection.
evidence_url_or_command: https://www.w3.org/TR/CSP3/ (meta element section); experiment in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-johnsolly-code-jsolly-website/8907a598-cb6b-487a-8acb-089323998de1/scratchpad/merge-plan/clones/platform/jsolly-website (meta contained frame-ancestors 'none';report-uri ...;sandbox)
plan_implication: frame-ancestors (and X-Frame-Options) must stay in the Vercel response header. Ban frame-ancestors/report-uri/sandbox from Astro csp directives with a build test. Because header and meta policies INTERSECT, the Vercel header must not carry img-src/font-src/style-src that are narrower than any page's meta (today the header has img-src 'self' data: and style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', which would block blog external https images even if the meta allows them). Move those resource directives out of the header into Astro csp, keeping the header to frame-ancestors + upgrade-insecure-requests.

question: 14. Service worker whose script URL starts returning a redirect: update behavior; old SW and cached navigations; kill-switch pattern; Clear-Site-Data alternative
answer: SW spec: when fetching the TOP-LEVEL service worker script, 'Set request's redirect mode to "error"', so a redirect (301/308) on the script URL is a network error: the update job fails and the existing registration keeps its active worker (it keeps controlling clients; a failed update never removes it). The script response must also have a JavaScript MIME type or the update is rejected with SecurityError. The live recipe PWA (https://www.blogthedata.com/post/15-minute-dump-and-go-instant-pot-recipes/service-worker.js, Cache-Control: no-cache) is CACHE-FIRST: its fetch handler returns cache.match() for the recipe page and ~150 precached /_astro/*, /data/recipe-library.* and /media/* assets, so installed/returning users get the old app from cache even after the origin redirects, and the SW URL redirect would leave them there indefinitely. Update checks happen on navigation within scope (and at most every 24h) independent of the cache-first response. KILL SWITCH (Chrome/Workbox 'remove buggy service workers' guidance): serve a replacement SW at the IDENTICAL URL with install: self.skipWaiting(); activate: delete caches, self.registration.unregister(), clients.matchAll({type:'window', includeUncontrolled:true}) then client.navigate(client.url); NO fetch handler. After unregistration the forced navigation goes to the network and receives the 301 to https://www.jsolly.com/recipes/. Existing controlled clients stay controlled until they unload or navigate, hence the navigate() step. Clear-Site-Data: "storage" (also "cache", "executionContexts") unregisters service workers for the whole ORIGIN (not the path), HTTPS only, baseline since Sept 2023, MDN notes varying support; it only fires on a response the browser actually receives, and a SW-served cache hit never contacts the server, so it is only a supplement. Browsers also treat a 404/410 SW script differently by vendor (UNVERIFIED), so use a 200 JS tombstone.

question: 15. Google Search Console Change of Address: is moving blogthedata.com to a subpath of an existing domain supported? Requirements? How long to keep redirects?
answer: YES, supported: Google's Change of Address help says 'you can use the tool to migrate your site from one domain to a path within another domain. For instance, from example.com to example3.com/new/location/'. Requirements: you own BOTH properties in Search Console with the same account, both DOMAIN-level (not path-level properties), a 301 redirect from the old homepage to the new homepage, and the tool does not move subdomains automatically (a separate www.blogthedata.com property needs its own request). Not for http->https, www/non-www, or same-domain moves. Keep redirects at least 180 days, Google's site-move guide says 'generally at least 1 year', ideally as long as possible; keep paying for the old domain at least a year. Google recommends one-to-one mapping, never mass-redirecting to the homepage. Both zones carry a google-site-verification TXT record in Cloudflare (blogthedata.com and jsolly.com), which suggests DNS-verified domain properties, but which property type/account holds them is UNVERIFIED.

question: 16. Feed readers: 301 on feed URL; GUID / Atom id stability
answer: RSS Advisory Board recommends the server answer old-feed requests with HTTP 301 and says readers should honor it (honoring is not guaranteed across readers, so also keep the old feed content reachable if possible). Atom: RFC 4287 4.2.6: 'When an Atom Document is relocated, migrated, syndicated, republished, exported, or imported, the content of its atom:id element MUST NOT change.' Live feeds: https://www.blogthedata.com/rss/ (RSS 2.0, 200 application/rss+xml; /rss -> 308 /rss/) and /atom/ (Atom, 200). RSS item <guid> (isPermaLink default true) = https://www.blogthedata.com/post/<slug>/ and Atom <id> = the same URL, so a naive new feed at jsolly.com/blog/ that derives guid/id from its own permalink changes EVERY item's identity.
evidence_url_or_command: https://www.rssboard.org/redirect-rss-feed; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4287#section-4.2.6; live curl https://www.blogthedata.com/rss/ and /atom/ (guid and id values); autodiscovery <link rel=alternate> hrefs /rss/ and /atom/ in the homepage
plan_implication: The new feeds must keep each legacy item's identity: emit <guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.blogthedata.com/post/<slug>/</guid> and Atom <id> = the old URL for all pre-merge posts (new posts may use jsolly URLs). 301 /rss/ -> https://www.jsolly.com/blog/rss/ (or chosen path) and /atom/ -> .../atom/. Do the feed redirects first in the list and test them with a feed-reader Accept header. Note the middleware 406 hazard for extensionless feed paths.

question: 20. (extra) Cutover verification mechanics: stage, test on generated URL, promote; rollback limits on Hobby
answer: STAGING: Project Settings > Environments > Production > Branch Tracking > 'Auto-assign Custom Production Domains' can be turned off (no plan restriction stated in the docs); a production deployment then stays 'Staged' and is promoted manually without a rebuild (`vercel promote`/dashboard Promote). CLI alternative: `vercel deploy --prod --skip-domain`. A deployment that has already been promoted cannot be promoted again (use rollback). Generated URLs are protected by Vercel Authentication (ssoProtection all_except_custom_domains), so verification needs `vercel curl --deployment <url>` or a bypass token; custom domains are public. ROLLBACK: Instant Rollback re-points domains to an earlier deployment without rebuild, but on HOBBY only to the immediately previous deployment (docs: 'Hobby users can roll back to the immediately previous deployment'; Pro/Enterprise any previously aliased deployment). After a rollback Vercel turns OFF auto-assignment of production domains until 'Undo rollback' (promote). GO-LIVE SWITCH: with auto-assign ON, connecting the project to jsolly-website makes the next push to main (any commit, even unrelated) publish the redirect-only site to blogthedata.com.
evidence_url_or_command: https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/promoting-a-deployment (staging section: 'turn off the auto-assignment of domains'; 'This option won't trigger a rebuild'; 'If a deployment has already been promoted in the past, you can't promote it again'); https://vercel.com/docs/instant-rollback ('Hobby users can roll back to the immediately previous deployment'; 'After a rollback, Vercel turns off auto-assignment of production domains'); https://vercel.com/docs/cli/deploying-from-cli ('Deploy with skipped domain assignment'); https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/promote-preview-to-production (vercel curl handles deployment protection)
plan_implication: Runbook order for John: (1) land legacy/blogthedata and the tombstone on main while the project is still connected to awesome-blog (no effect on blogthedata.com); (2) turn OFF auto-assign for the blogthedata project BEFORE connecting jsolly-website; (3) disconnect awesome-blog, connect jsolly-website (Root Directory legacy/blogthedata); (4) trigger a staged deployment (push or redeploy), run the URL-map test with `vercel curl` against the generated URL; (5) promote; (6) verify in production with the real domains; (7) re-enable auto-assign only after verification (or keep manual promote for redirect edits); (8) archive awesome-blog last. Connecting the Git source is the go-live trigger when auto-assign is on, so step 2 must precede step 3. If a second redirect-only deployment is needed before verification finishes, the awesome-blog deployment is no longer rollback-able on Hobby; the fallback is to reconnect awesome-blog (still unarchived) and redeploy main.

question: 22. (extra) robots.txt and sitemap handling on the retired host

A Disallow on the retired host would stop Google from crawling the 301s and delay consolidation. Live blogthedata.com currently serves /robots.txt (200) and /sitemap.xml (200); /sitemap-index.xml is 404; feed URLs are /rss/ and /atom/.
